title: fix(app-shell): read a stored $gt back as the operator the column offers
body:
Fixes #9382

The card asked for a measurement before a shape, and the triage seat made that the first deliverable. Both readings are below; the shape argument rests on them.

## Reading (i) — the census

Over the whole domain the dropdown can build — every field type this inspector draws, crossed with the operators that type's bucket offers — each row was built the way an author builds it, stored, and reopened.

**122 pairs built, 116 round-tripped exactly, 6 broke.** All six are the same two operators on the three date-like types:

```
date       before  -> $lt -> lessThan      NOT OFFERED BY THIS BUCKET
date       after   -> $gt -> greaterThan   NOT OFFERED BY THIS BUCKET
datetime   before  -> $lt -> lessThan      NOT OFFERED BY THIS BUCKET
datetime   after   -> $gt -> greaterThan   NOT OFFERED BY THIS BUCKET
time       before  -> $lt -> lessThan      NOT OFFERED BY THIS BUCKET
time       after   -> $gt -> greaterThan   NOT OFFERED BY THIS BUCKET
```

The control the card's own body insists on is lit: `greaterThan` IS a member of the number bucket, so the `false` on the date bucket is a reading about dates specifically and not a lookup that answers `false` for everything.

**Extension to the card.** The card and the claim both say "a date column". Measured, the blast radius is **three** field types, not one — `dateLikeTypes` carries `date`, `datetime` and `time`, and all three offer `before` / `after`. `time` in particular is not obvious from the card.

**The ambiguity is not unique, and the other two cases are the argument for the repair.** Counting preimages under the write half: four tokens have two operators writing them — `$exists`, `$null`, `$gt`, `$lt`. The first two are already disambiguated, by their PAYLOAD, in this same function: the stored value is the boolean that picks between `isEmpty` / `isNotEmpty` and `isNull` / `isNotNull`. `$gt` / `$lt` carry the author's comparand instead, so no bit of the stored condition can tell `after` from `greaterThan`. This file already resolves ambiguous tokens rather than guessing; two of its four cases just happened to have a disambiguator in the payload.

## Reading (ii) — the consequence the card did NOT drive

Driven in the real component, through the real round trip. Reopened row, date column:

```
author picked   : after
stored          : {"closed_at":{"$gt":"2026-01-01"}}
row reads back  : greaterThan
TRIGGER RENDERS : ""          (the empty string: a BLANK trigger)
control, number column, same token:
TRIGGER RENDERS : "Greater than"
```

So the card's guess was right and triage's question is answered: **a control the author cannot read**, not cosmetic drift.

**It is worse than the card guessed, and this was not in either document.** The blank row is still live. Measured:

```
reconcileOperatorForField('greaterThan', dateBucket) = equals
onChange calls after a plain re-open                 = 0
```

Reopening alone writes nothing back — the stored filter survives being looked at. But the moment the author touches that row's **field** picker, the builder's own reconcile step cannot find the unlisted operator in the new bucket and settles the row on `equals`, then commits it. An "after this date" filter silently becomes an "equals this date" filter, with no error and no visible cause. The blank trigger is the symptom; the reconcile is the data loss behind it.

## Which shape, and why the other two stay fenced

**B — make the read half field-type-aware.** Taken.

The decisive point is that the stored bytes are **not** wrong. The spec's `FILTER_OPERATORS` carries exactly one token for "strictly greater" and there is no `$after`; the filter this bridge stored filters correctly. What was lost is only the LABEL — and the label is a function of the field's declared type, because that is what decides which bucket the dropdown draws. Type is schema information, not filter data. Recovering it from the schema is therefore the contract-respecting direction; pushing it onto the wire is not.

Concretely: `conditionToGroup` takes the same `fields` list the inspector already hands the builder, and settles an ambiguous token against that field's own bucket. The bucket table is **asked, not copied** — `operatorsForFieldType` is called with no opt-in extras, exactly as the inspector mounts the builder — so the read-back operator cannot disagree with what the dropdown actually lists. A second copy of that relation in app-shell is precisely the drift this file's own docblocks warn about.

This is not a lenient fallback. Nothing new is accepted, no stored filter is rewritten, and the write half is untouched. When the type is unknown, the field is absent from the list, or the bucket offers neither candidate, the read falls back to the unchanged fixed table.

**A — give `after` / `before` their own tokens.** Not taken, and **doubly** fenced. The claim fences it on objectui#9306 being open. Independently measured here: the spec's `FILTER_OPERATORS` is `$eq $ne $gt $gte $lt $lte $in $nin $between $contains $notContains $startsWith $endsWith $icontains $null $exists` — there is no `$after` and no `$before`, so A is not an objectui change at all. It would need a vocabulary change in `@objectstack/spec`, a different repository.

**C — add `greaterThan` / `lessThan` to the date bucket.** Not taken. Fenced by the claim as `@object-ui/components`' call, and the measurement independently argues against it: C does not end the collapse, it only makes the wrong answer a **listed** one. The author would still pick `After` and reopen to `Greater than` — converting the harm from "blank trigger" into "silently wrong but plausible operator", which is the worse of the two harms triage named. `@object-ui/components` is untouched by this branch; its buckets are read, never changed.

## The pin, and that it fails on the pre-fix tree

`datasetFilterCondition.dateRoundTrip-9382.test.tsx` goes through the round trip — build the row, store it, reopen it — rather than asserting either mapping table, and asserts the operator the bucket actually offers.

Reverse verification, run from the committed fix: the two implementation files were restored to the pre-fix tree (`f0b497921`) with the pin left in place, proven on disk (blob hashes differ; the `readBackOperator` anchor goes 5 to 0, the call-site anchor 1 to 0), then restored from `HEAD` and proven clean (`git diff HEAD` empty).

Predicted before running, and observed:

```
Tests  9 failed | 6 passed (15)
```

The 9 are exactly the predicted ones — the 6 round-trip pairs, the whole-domain invariant, and the 2 driven renders:

```
AssertionError: expected 'greaterThan' to be 'after'
AssertionError: expected 'lessThan' to be 'before'
AssertionError: expected '' to be 'After'
AssertionError: expected '' to be 'Before'
expected [ 'date/before -> lessThan', ...(5) ] to deeply equal []
```

The 6 that stayed green are exactly the two `controls` and the four `boundaries the repair must not cross` — green in both directions by construction, carried as over-reach guards and labelled in the file as not pins.

Two guards against the failure modes this lane has paid for: the round-trip answer is asserted to be a non-empty string before it is compared, so the membership test cannot pass by comparing two absences; and the whole-domain sweep asserts its own denominator, so a suite that silently stopped building rows could not read as a clean sweep.

## Verification

All through the shared serialisation lock.

| run | result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/app-shell^...' build` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/` | 82 files, 1000 passed, 1 skipped, exit 0 |
| new pin, post-fix | 15 passed |
| new pin, pre-fix tree | 9 failed, 6 passed |

Gates, all exit 0: `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:phantom-deps`, and `check-changeset-presence.mjs`.

The inspectors directory run is the affected surface: it contains every caller of this bridge, including the three sibling pins that call `conditionToGroup` with no field list. They pass unchanged, which is the fallback arm being exercised.

Lint is narrowed deliberately and the narrowing is measured, not merely unrun: ESLint on the 3 changed files reports **0 errors, 6 warnings**, and all 6 sit on pre-existing lines (the `cond as any` / `c as any` casts and the `fields as any` prop, all present at `f0b497921`). The narrowing is sound because this repo's ESLint config enables no type-aware linting — no `projectService` and no `parserOptions.project` — so this diff cannot move the verdict on any file it does not contain. The repo-level scan stays CI's.

Measurements were taken at `1311e8a7d`.

## Acceptance notes

Out of scope, noted and deliberately not filed:

- The same `dateLikeTypes` fan-out means `time` columns are affected identically to `date`. Covered by this branch, recorded here because both the card and the claim describe the defect as a date-column one.
- `content/docs/plugins/plugin-report.mdx` documents `runtimeFilter: { last_activity_date: { $lt: daysAgo(60) } }` — a date column carrying the ambiguous token. It is a doc example of a runtime filter, not a stored dataset filter edited through this inspector, so it is not a second instance of this defect and needs no change. Successor: none — no PR or person is heading for that file on account of this.
- The `filter-builder.tsx` docblock claims the canonical fold is injective over the builder's vocabulary. Re-measured here and it holds: all 22 ids fold to 22 distinct canonical operators, and `after` / `before` fold to themselves rather than onto `greater_than` / `less_than`. Recorded because objectui#9306 discusses that folding as an open question, and the answer on today's tree is that the spec's fold does **not** perform it.
